samples.summary: The proxied-hop "pin drop" is attacker-triggerable by document content, so a malicious image `src` can hand DNS resolution back to the egress proxy and reach addresses the SSRF gate refused (contradicting the "not attacker-triggerable" claim in the code comment and design doc).
samples.evidence: `rawRequest` (line 662-670) converts *any* rejection from `undiciRequest` into `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')` — proxy answering CONNECT with 403/502, CONNECT timeout, TLS failure, socket reset, origin unreachable. The catch at line 800-812 accepts every one of those as proof that "the proxy refuses address literals": it sets the fetcher-wide `pinThroughProxy = false` (line 808) and immediately re-issues the SAME target with `planHop(target, addresses, false)` (line 810), which returns a plain `ProxyAgent` with the original hostname, i.e. the proxy now resolves the name itself. Attack, on any machine with `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`all_proxy` set (the only machines this path exists for): attacker puts `` in a document a victim exports with `docs export --format pdf` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:281). (1) The gate resolves `rebind.attacker.tld` via the CLI's resolver and gets an attacker-chosen public address, so it is approved and returned as the pin. (2) The pinned hop asks the proxy for that literal; the attacker guarantees this fails — point the gate-visible answer at a blackholed/closed public address of their own, or at an address the proxy's egress ACL denies (exactly the 403-to-literal shape modelled in packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:844-851). (3) undici rejects → NETWORK_ERROR → line 808 disables pinning and line 812 retries by NAME through the proxy. (4) The attacker's ~0s-TTL nameserver now answers the proxy with `169.254.169.254` (or an RFC1918 host on the proxy's network); the proxy connects there and the bytes are embedded in the PDF/DOCX/PPTX the victim opens. The gate's per-address verdict is fully bypassed for that hop, and `pinThroughProxy` stays false for every remaining image in the export (test at line 867-902 asserts precisely that persistence: image two never retries the address form). The comment at image-fetcher.ts:511-513 ("The fallback is not attacker-triggerable: whether the proxy accepts an address literal is a property of the environment, not of the document") and docs/design/cli.md:1113-1115 assert the opposite of what the catch condition implements: the document chooses the address the proxy is asked for and can therefore choose to make the pinned attempt fail. A safe form would restrict the fallback to the specific proxy-refusal signal (e.g. a 403/405 CONNECT response) rather than any NETWORK_ERROR, and/or re-gate the retry by requiring the name to resolve to an approved address again with the pin re-armed per hop.

samples.summary: `rawRequest` interpolates the raw transport error message into the SystemError, skipping the `redactDetail` scrubbing `fetchOrThrow` applies — a presigned image `src` query string can land on stderr/CI logs.
samples.evidence: errors.ts:126-138 exists specifically because "undici and Node echo the request URL verbatim for some failures", and `fetchOrThrow` runs every transport error message through `redactDetail(detail, url)` (errors.ts:167). `rawRequest` in image-fetcher.ts:663-669 builds its own SystemError with `redactUrl(target)` for the URL but `cause.message` VERBATIM, and `redactDetail` is not exported so this path cannot use it. Image `src` values "routinely carry presigned tokens in the query string" (errors.ts:88-92); any undici error whose message quotes the request URL therefore prints the token that `redactUrl` was added to strip. Reachable on both the pinned-proxy path (image-fetcher.ts:766) and the opaque-redirect fallback (line 780).

samples.summary: `isPrivateAddress` does not recognise IPv4-translated addresses (`::ffff:0:0/96`, e.g. `::ffff:0:7f00:1`) or NAT64 prefixes other than the well-known `64:ff9b::/96`, so such a DNS answer is judged public and pinned as allowed.
samples.evidence: The v4-embedded checks all require `words.slice(0,5)` to be zero (line 167) or a specific leading word (0x0064, 0x2002, 0x2001). `::ffff:0:127.0.0.1` normalises to `::ffff:0:7f00:1` → words `[0,0,0,0,0xffff,0,0x7f00,1]`; `words[4] !== 0` so the loopback/embedded-v4 branch is skipped, none of the transition-prefix branches match, and the function returns false. An attacker-controlled AAAA record returning such an address (or an address inside a site's own NAT64 prefix, which is operator-chosen and not the well-known one) passes the gate and is then *pinned* as approved. I could not confirm a host that actually routes `::ffff:0:0/96` to IPv4, so exploitability is unproven — hence low confidence — but the gate's stated rule ("in any spelling", line 160) is not met.

samples.summary: `printDryRun` prints the configured server URL verbatim on stdout, including any userinfo credentials, instead of passing it through `redactUrl`.
samples.evidence: `config.server` may carry userinfo — errors.ts:87-89 states `--server`/`WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` "may carry userinfo (https://user:pass@host)" and that is why `redactUrl` exists. dry-run.ts:12-13 builds `url` from `config.server` unmodified and `console.log`s it (line 24), so `--dry-run` output captured in a CI log or a shared terminal reproduces the credential. Every other stderr/stdout site in the CLI routes URLs through `redactUrl`; this one does not.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. rawRequest collapses every undici rejection into SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR') (image-fetcher.ts:662-670), and the pin-drop catch accepts any such error as proof the proxy refuses address literals (image-fetcher.ts:800-806), then sets the fetcher-wide pinThroughProxy = false (808) and re-issues the same target via planHop(target, addresses, false) (810), which returns a bare ProxyAgent with the original hostname and no connector pin (536-543), handing DNS resolution to the proxy. Because the document chooses the src host, it chooses the address the proxy is asked to CONNECT to and can guarantee that attempt fails (blackholed/closed public address, or one the proxy ACL denies — the 403-to-literal shape modelled at test/image-fetcher.test.ts:844-851), so the fallback IS attacker-triggerable, contradicting the comment at 511-513. The gate's per-address verdict is then bypassed for that hop and, since the flag is per-fetcher (735), for every remaining image in the export (asserted at test/image-fetcher.test.ts:894-897). Reachable from `docs export` (commands/docs.ts:281) and `slides export` (commands/slides.ts:224) on any machine with http_proxy/https_proxy/all_proxy set. The stderr warning (736-749) notifies but does not guard, and misattributes the cause to the environment. This is an SSRF-gate weakening in the security lane, and blocking under this rubric.
